lyrics:
[Intro: fingerpicked open-string electric guitar, alone]

[Verse 1: low weathered male voice, quiet]
I used to keep a hundred fires
Had to win, had to be seen
Every room a thing to conquer
Every man a thing to beat

[Verse 2: second guitar and bass enter]
Then the years came through like weather
Took the hair and took the pride
Took my father, took my hurry
Left a few things by my side

[Chorus: strings swell, voice stronger]
And the list got short
Three names and a dog
A porch, a little time
The list got short
And everything I dropped
Was never really mine

[Verse 3: drums enter, steady]
I don't need the last word anymore
I don't need to hold the floor
I know who I would run back for
I don't need a whole lot more

[Chorus: full band and orchestra]
And the list got short
Three names and a dog
A porch, a little time
The list got short
And everything I dropped
Was never really mine

[Guitar Solo: long, singing, melodic, over the orchestra]

[Bridge: band drops low, voice close]
Ask me what I'm proud of
I'll point across the room

[Final Chorus: biggest, then down to one guitar]
The list got short
Three names and a dog
A porch, a little time
The list got short
And everything I kept
Is here, and it is mine

[Outro: the opening guitar pattern, alone, slowing]
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 69 BPM, 6/8, E minor. Slow, grave and patient, growing from one guitar to a full orchestra.

VOICE: Male baritone, low, rough and restrained, sung gently with almost no vibrato, as if he does not usually sing this quietly. He pushes harder in the later choruses but never screams.

INSTRUMENTS: A clean electric guitar fingerpicking open strings, a second guitar with harmonics, bass, a drum kit that enters late and plays simply, a full string section and French horns, a lead guitar with a warm, sustained tone for the solo.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, guitar alone. 0:28 Verse 1. 1:00 Verse 2. 1:30 Chorus 1. 2:00 Verse 3, drums in. 2:30 Chorus 2. 3:00 Guitar solo. 3:44 Bridge. 4:02 Final chorus. 4:36 Outro, guitar alone, ends 4:58.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Early-1990s rock ballad with orchestra: warm, deep and spacious, guitars clean, drums big and slow.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The guitar solo entering at 3:00.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The original is a young man discovering that one relationship matters more than his armour. This is the same discovery made at fifty-five, when it applies to nearly everything he once chased.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Restless, stripped, clear, content.
